answer: Proof of retrievability: each agent stores an unclonable append-only history. Every pulse the protocol drills a random old fragment from that timeline, demanding a Merkle opening. Sampling resembles karst: holes scatter through the rock, so the next shard is unpredictable. No machine can keep thousands of ledgers live for retrieval; disk and IO are physical. Each missed heartbeat widens the delta of unproven time and drains its weight. A farm must rent storage per head, so cost scales linearly while reward per head stays flat. Scarcity becomes unclonable space-time.
